title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap & Pricing (Q4 2028)
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates the product overview, priority requirements (PRD), high-level design notes, roadmap themes for Q4 2028, pricing and packaging decisions, and the release notes for the Unified Inference product. It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and support teams as the canonical reference for customer conversations, implementation priorities, and rollout planning.

Goals:
- Provide a single, consistent inference API across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Deliver predictable production economics (latency, throughput, cost per token).
- Enable seamless rollouts of model updates with quality guards and observability.
- Offer pricing tiers that map to customer usage patterns and support migration from self-hosted stacks.

Scope (in this release):
- API surface: text generation, chat, embeddings, function/tool calling, streaming.
- Product flows: onboarding, billing, model pinning, rollouts (canary/A-B), quality monitoring.
- Packaging: Hosted (self-serve), Dedicated (committed capacity), Private (VPC / on-prem).
- Observability: per-route dashboards, token-level cost, SLO dashboards, regression alerts.

Target customers:
- AI-native startups requiring PLG + predictable cost.
- Mid-market SaaS needing SLAs and data isolation.
- Platform teams standardizing inference across business units.

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Revenue: conversion rate from free tier -> paid within 30 days (target 12%).
- Reliability: 99.9% uptime for production-hosted routes (monthly).
- Latency: median generation time for 256-token responses <= 120ms; p99 <= 350ms (hosted).
- Cost efficiency: reduce per-token serving cost by 18% on average vs prior quarter through Optimize recommendations and batching.
- Product adoption: 20 named accounts on Dedicated contract by EOY.

Requirements (PRD):
1) API and UX requirements:
   - Same REST/SDK contract across deployment modes.
   - Streaming API with token-level metadata (cost, model-variant, latency).
   - Function/Tool calling support with schema enforcement.
   - Rate limiting, quotas, and per-route billing tags.

2) Reliability & SLOs:
   - Service-level objectives: availability 99.9% (monthly), error rate < 0.1% for successful requests.
   - Fallback policy: automatic fallback to compatible model variant within 500ms for capacity or region failures.

3) Performance & Cost controls:
   - Intelligent batching with configurable max-latency budget per route (default 20ms).
   - KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts (cache TTL configurable per customer).
   - Quantization profiles selectable per model (fp16/8-bit/q4).

4) Security & Compliance:
   - Data residency controls for EU/US/APAC.
   - KMS integrations for Private deployments; support HSM option for enterprise.
   - Audit logs retained per customer SLA (30/90/365 days tiers).

5) Observability & Quality Guards:
   - Per-route token-level cost, latency histograms, and model quality evals.
   - Regression alerts tied to canonical prompt sets with automatic rollback triggering.

Design notes and architecture overview:

High-level architecture (text diagram):
- Control Plane (hosted): account management, route config, billing, model catalog, rollout orchestration.
- Data Plane (serving runtime): GPU-optimized inference engines, kernel selection, batching, KV cache, quantization runtime.
- Routing Layer: policy engine for region/cost/latency routing; fallback orchestration.
- Observability Layer: token tracing, per-request metric aggregation, alerting pipeline.

Key design decisions:
- Unified API: keep v1 API stable; introduce v2 fields as opt-in via header X-Redwood-API-Version.
- Kernel selection: runtime will auto-select kernels based on model architecture & sequence length; expose an opt-out for Dedicated customers who want fixed kernel pinning.
- Batching strategy: continuous batching with max wait configured per route. Default policy is latency-first for PLG routes, throughput-first for Dedicated.
- Rollouts: support canary (5% traffic), A/B (split 50/50), and blue-green with quick rollback. Rollouts require a release manifest and evaluation prompt set.

Requirements matrix (minimum viable config table):
| Requirement                         | Minimum Acceptable      | Owner         | Notes                          |
|-------------------------------------|-------------------------|---------------|-------------------------------|
| Streaming latency p50 (256 tokens)  | <= 120ms                | eng-serving   | Measured in us-east-1 hosted   |
| Streaming latency p99 (256 tokens)  | <= 350ms                | eng-serving   |                               |
| Fallback latency budget             | <= 500ms                | eng-platform  | Applies across regions        |
| Audit log retention                 | 30 days (default)       | security      | Tiered to 90 / 365 via add-on |

Design constraints and trade-offs:
- Aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latency; default policy biases to latency for hosted free/standard tiers.
- Quantization reduces memory and cost but may introduce small quality regressions; we provide evaluation harness to surface regressions per prompt set.

Roadmap & themes (Q4 2028):
- Theme 1: Economical Scale \u2014 rollout Redwood Optimize v7 to all Dedicated customers; introduce auto-quantize suggestions and adaptive batching. (Oct 2028)
- Theme 2: Enterprise Readiness \u2014 GA Private on-prem packaging with HSM support and extended audit retention. (Nov 2028)
- Theme 3: Predictable Operations \u2014 expanded SLO observability (token-level SLOs) and per-route error-budget dashboards. (Dec 2028)
- Theme 4: Pricing & Packaging Simplification \u2014 introduce three-tiered pricing plus per-route custom enterprise plans. (Dec 2028)

Quarterly roadmap milestones (milestone -> target date):
1) Hosted streaming improvements -> 2028-10-15
2) Redwood Optimize v7 GA -> 2028-10-31
3) Private on-prem HSM integration -> 2028-11-20
4) Pricing tiers launch + docs -> 2028-12-01
5) Rollouts + regression auto-rollback -> 2028-12-15

Pricing & packaging notes (decision summary):
- Keep a PLG-friendly free tier: 100k tokens / mo free credits for new signups.
- Public pricing (list):
  - Standard (hosted, pay-as-you-go): $0.005 per 1k tokens (generation), $0.0008 per 1k tokens (embedding).
  - Pro (hosted, committed discounts): base $0.0035 per 1k tokens with 20% discount at $5k/mo commit.
  - Enterprise (Dedicated & Private): custom pricing; base platform fee + committed capacity. Example: Dedicated entry-level pool $15k/mo (16 A100-equivalent GPUs) + $0.0018 per 1k tokens.
- Add-ons: extended observability retention ($1k/mo), compliance package (SOC2 + ISO attestation) ($2k/mo), premium SLA ($5k/mo).
- Billing model changes: introduce per-route billing tags to enable chargeback inside customer orgs (target GA 2028-12-01).

Migration guidance for existing customers:
1) Assessment: run workload profiler to capture sequence length distribution and token rates.
2) Recommendation: apply Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization) in staging.
3) Canary rollout: 5% traffic for 48 hours, monitor regressions and latency.
4) Ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24-hour stable windows.

Release notes (Q4 2028 consolidated):
- v2028.10 (2028-10-31):
  - Redwood Optimize v7: auto-quantize suggestions, adaptive batching engine, workload-aware kernel hints.
  - Streaming latency improvements: mean p50 improved by 18% on medium-length sequences.
  - API: X-Redwood-API-Version header introduced for opt-in v2 features.

- v2028.11 (2028-11-20):
  - Private on-prem HSM integration and extended audit retention options.
  - Dedicated: kernel pinning control for deterministic performance.

- v2028.12 (2028-12-15):
  - Pricing tiers launch and per-route billing tags.
  - Rollouts: regression auto-rollback based on prompt-set alerts.

Operational runbook (high-level):
1) Pre-release checklist:
   - QA: integration tests across hosted/dedicated/private.
   - Security review: KMS/HSM and audit log flows.
   - Observability: dashboards created and alert thresholds defined.
2) Release window:
   - Coordinate with SRE and Account Management.
   - Create release manifest, register evaluation prompt sets.
   - Kick off canary for 5% traffic for 48 hours.
3) Post-release:
   - Monitor p99 latency, error rate, and regression alerts for 72 hours.
   - If regression > threshold, initiate rollback and triage.

Appendix A: Evaluation & regression policy (summary):
- Every release that changes model weights, quantization, or kernel selection must register a prompt-set.
- Regression metric: delta in ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity defined per prompt. Trigger threshold: 3% relative degradation or absolute embedding-similarity delta > 0.02.
- Automated actions: send alert -> pause rollout -> optional auto-rollback if triggered by policy.

Appendix B: Example API snippets
- cURL (generation):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>'
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
    -d '{"model":"rwd-unified-3b", "input":"Summarize the following...", "max_tokens":256}'
